title: Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2026 goes to the discoverers of optogenetics
summary: Karl Deisseroth of the Howard Hughes Medical Institute and Stanford University, Peter Hegemann of Humboldt University of Berlin and Georg Nagel of the University of Würzburg share the prize. Hegemann and Nagel found channelrhodopsin, a light-sensitive protein in a single-celled alga; Deisseroth turned it into a switch that lets researchers turn individual nerve cells on and off with light.
why: Optogenetics is now a standard tool in neuroscience labs, and funded PhDs in neuroscience and neuroengineering often use it.

title: Three doctoral fellowships in AI and robotics open at ETH Zurich
summary: ETH Zurich is recruiting for its AI Center Doctoral Fellowship (8 to 12 places, closing 27 October), the Max Planck ETH Center for Learning Systems (closing 2 November) and the RobotX PhD Fellowship in robotics (closing 15 December).
why: All three are funded doctoral routes into AI and robotics at one of Europe's leading technical universities.
source_title: ETH Zurich — Jobs: ETH AI Center Doctoral Fellowship 2027

title: Chevening Scholarships for 2027–28 close on 6 October at 11:00 UTC
summary: Applications for the UK government's fully funded one-year master's scholarships close on 6 October 2026 at 11:00 UTC, after which the online system shuts. Shortlisting for interviews follows in mid-February 2027.
why: 11:00 UTC is 11:00 in Accra, 12:00 in London and Lagos, 14:00 in Nairobi, 16:30 in Delhi and 07:00 in New York, so check your own time zone.

title: Lasker Awards 2026: the brain's wakefulness signal, and a new treatment for haemophilia A
summary: Emmanuel Mignot of Stanford University and Masashi Yanagisawa of the University of Tsukuba won the basic research award for identifying orexin, the brain peptide that keeps us awake, and showing that its loss causes narcolepsy. Three scientists at Chugai Pharmaceutical in Tokyo won the clinical award for an antibody that restores blood clotting in haemophilia A, and Michael J. Fox the public service award for his work on Parkinson's disease.
why: The Lasker Awards are often called America's Nobels, and many laureates later receive a Nobel Prize.

title: Fields Medals 2026 for Yu Deng, John Pardon, Jacob Tsimerman and Hong Wang
summary: Mathematics' highest honour for researchers under 40 was announced at the opening of the International Congress of Mathematicians in Philadelphia. The work it recognises ranges from deriving the equations of gases and waves, through symplectic geometry and arithmetic geometry, to harmonic analysis and the Kakeya problem in three dimensions.
why: Hong Wang is only the third woman to receive the Fields Medal, after Maryam Mirzakhani in 2014 and Maryna Viazovska in 2022.

title: Kavli Prizes 2026: how the Milky Way was built, 'twistronics', and protein-making in neurons
summary: The astrophysics prize went to Vasily Belokurov, Amina Helmi and Rodrigo Ibata for showing that our galaxy grew by swallowing smaller ones. The nanoscience prize went to Eva Andrei, Pablo Jarillo-Herrero and Allan MacDonald for founding twistronics, which changes a material's properties by twisting atom-thin layers. The neuroscience prize went to Christine Holt, Kelsey Martin, Erin Schuman and Oswald Steward for showing that neurons make proteins locally, where they are needed. Each prize is worth US$1 million.
why: Twistronics and galactic archaeology are young, fast-growing fields in physics and astronomy.

title: Breakthrough Prizes 2026: gene therapies, ALS genetics and the muon's magnetism
summary: Three life-sciences prizes honoured the first FDA-approved gene therapy for an inherited disease (a form of blindness), the switch from fetal to adult haemoglobin behind new sickle-cell treatments, and the most common genetic cause of ALS and frontotemporal dementia. Frank Merle won in mathematics, and the Muon g-2 collaborations at CERN, Brookhaven and Fermilab in fundamental physics. Each prize is worth US$3 million.
why: Gene therapy and precision measurement are both areas where universities are hiring funded PhD students.

title: Abel Prize 2026 to Gerd Faltings for his work in arithmetic geometry
summary: The Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters awarded the prize to Gerd Faltings of the Max Planck Institute for Mathematics in Bonn, for powerful new tools in arithmetic geometry and for settling long-standing conjectures of Mordell and Lang about whole-number solutions to equations. He is the first German to receive it.
why: Faltings's 1983 proof of the Mordell conjecture is one of the landmark results of modern number theory.
source_title: The Abel Prize — Gerd Faltings awarded the 2026 Abel Prize

title: Turing Award goes to the founders of quantum information science
summary: ACM named Charles Bennett of IBM Research and Gilles Brassard of the Université de Montréal as recipients of the 2025 A.M. Turing Award. In 1984 they introduced BB84, the first practical protocol for quantum cryptography, and in 1993, with colleagues, quantum teleportation. The award carries US$1 million.
why: Quantum computing and quantum security now offer funded PhDs across Europe and North America, including the Uppsala quantum verification post on our positions page.
